# v1.4.1 — Maintenance and dependency updates

This maintenance release brings together the dependency repairs and compatibility
checks since v1.4.0. It adds no database migrations or required environment
variables. Existing event links, RSVP edit links, and text limits are preserved.

## Changes

- Refresh the dependency security baseline, including Next.js 16.3.6,
  Sharp 0.35.4, Nodemailer 9.1.1, html-to-text 10.0.1, and patched transitive
  dependencies. Keep the checked-in lockfiles and compatibility overrides.
- Update React and React DOM together to 19.3.0, Prisma to 7.10.0, and Zod to
  4.6.5. Preserve the app's existing UTF-16 text limits across Zod's Unicode
  length change, with regression coverage for emoji and other non-BMP text.
- Refresh development tooling, including Playwright 1.63.0 and its matching
  browser image, Vitest/coverage 5.0.2, and Node 22 type declarations.
- Align the optional email worker's Cloudflare types with its tooling and retain
  the patched Sharp override. The worker API is unchanged; this release does
  not deploy the worker.
- Verify production containers on native AMD64 and ARM64 runners, including
  startup, migrations, seeding, storage permissions, health, image codecs, and
  restoring a startup backup into a disposable database.
- Restrict image publishing to owner-initiated releases and reruns. Prereleases
  now receive only their exact version tag and cannot move `latest` or `1.4`.
- Correct the installation and upgrade commands to select the prebuilt-image
  Compose file explicitly and preserve data during routine image rollback.

## Upgrade from v1.4.0

1. Back up the database, uploads, and `.env`; record the running image digest.
2. In your deployment Compose file, pin the app image to
   `ghcr.io/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me:1.4.1` after the Release workflow has published it.
   Container tags omit the Git release tag's leading `v`.
3. With the standard production configuration, run:

   ```bash
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml pull app
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up -d --no-deps app
   docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml logs --tail=100 app
   ```

4. Check health, sign-in, event creation, public/protected RSVPs, RSVP editing,
   uploads, and delivery through the email/SMS providers enabled on your site.

Run these commands in the existing deployment directory with its existing
project name, mounts, and secrets. If you use a custom Compose file, retain that
configuration and update only the app image. This maintenance upgrade does not
require upgrading PostgreSQL or Redis.

For Docker installations, Node 22 is included in the image. Source installations
must use the repository's supported Node 22/npm 10 versions and reinstall from
the lockfiles. Dotenv 18 retains normal `.env` loading; custom tooling that used
dotenv's removed `.env.vault` or legacy `dotenv_config_*` CLI arguments needs a
separate adjustment. This repository uses neither removed interface.

## Rollback and known limitations

For a rollback to v1.4.0, pin the app to the previously recorded image digest
(or `ghcr.io/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me:1.4.0`) and recreate only the app container.
No schema changed in this release, so a routine rollback does not require a
database restore. Restoring an older backup would discard newer RSVPs.

Builds still download Google fonts through Next.js and can encounter the tracked
upstream font-query failure. Fonts are served locally at runtime. Provider
tests use mocks; passing CI does not confirm delivery through your live email
or SMS account.

See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/blob/main/docs/admin/upgrading.md)
for backup, verification, and release approval procedures.

**Full comparison:** https://github.com/joe-cole1/rsvp-to-me/compare/v1.4.0...v1.4.1
